research_concepts: counter strategy (PNR fail followed by PULL_UP)
play-type possession efficiency (PPP) by defensive unit
lift relative to baseline by unit
methodological_questions: How is 'PNR fail' operationalised from play-by-play and possession records, and is it defined before the PULL_UP outcome is observed?
Is lift measured as PPP after PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP minus a matched baseline, and does the baseline control for shot quality, opponent and game context?
What is the unit (defensive team x season, or team x season x PT), and how many units have enough PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP possessions to estimate lift?
Does the 70% of units with lift>0 and median lift >2pp rule survive shrinkage, placebo play types, and a falsification test on non-PNR-fail possessions?

historical_evidence.finding: Descriptive RS vs playoff comparison across 25 teams (min 30 possessions per cell). Records DRIVE allowed PPP 1.191 to 0.923 and PNR PPP change -0.139 with share +12.1pp, and PULL_UP PPP +0.341 with share -7.6pp. The record notes the PNR share jump may reflect tagging differences and that there was no inferential test. It is not conditioned on a PNR-fail trigger.

Shot-level PNR share of half-court shots by team in 2024-25 (30 teams, about 5,994 to 6,581 half-court shots per team). Shares range from about 7.6% (OKC) to 13.8% (IND). The record is descriptive, with no pass/fail gate and verdict 'descriptive', and it serves as a calibration input for a PNR proxy. The mechanism for failure is recorded as unclear.

Star-initiator suppression by lineup and forced play type (Jokic, Curry, Doncic, Giannis), with lineup PPP gaps reported (e.g., Giannis forced PULL_UP PPP 0.848 vs preferred DRIVE, gap -0.540, n not stated in the summary). Record notes no placebo or matching, and that later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts. It has an auto-identified risk of PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE.

Turnover-force adversarial channel: raw lifts shrink by roughly half under opponent re-routing and possession-tendency shifts (e.g., PHI +12.0 to +6.0pp, PHX +14.8 to +7.5pp). Net lift is model-implied, not observed; the counter check is often an additive surrogate at n<10. Based on 4 games and 8 offense-defense sides.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading lineup and forced-play-type PPP gaps as suppression effects without placebo, matching, or sequence controls
failed_approaches.why: Recorded failure mechanism is unclear; no placebo or matching was run, and later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts (auto risk PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Raw counter-channel lifts as robust effects
failed_approaches.why: Recorded that the R1 lifts shrink by about 50% or more once opponent re-route and possession shift are applied. Net lift is model-implied rather than observed, and the surrogate counter check is underpowered at n<10 (mechanism recorded as unclear).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using play-type PPP and share shifts between RS and playoffs as evidence of a defensive counter
failed_approaches.why: No inferential test was run. The PNR share jump of +12.1pp may reflect tagging differences, with records flagged for LABEL_ERROR and MECHANICAL_FLOOR risk (mechanism unclear).

evidence_establishes: The project has prior play-type possession records (Neo4j INITIATED edges) and descriptive PNR, PULL_UP and DRIVE PPP and share summaries by team, so the question can be framed on existing derived data.
PNR share and play-type tagging vary by team and between regular season and playoffs in ways the project has not yet validated (SF-APPM-058, SF-APPS-012).

Earlier counter and suppression claims in this project shrank substantially under robustness checks or were flagged as placebo-dependent (SF-APPA-067, SF-CHT-009), so a raw lift threshold is unlikely to be sufficient.
evidence_does_not_establish: Any inferential result for PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP lift. None of the four records conditions on a PNR-fail trigger or tests lift>0 across units.
Whether PNR fail is reliably identifiable in the play-by-play, or how it is tagged versus the PNR proxy.
The unit-level distribution of lift, so the 70% and median >2pp thresholds cannot be evaluated from history.
Whether PULL_UP lift is specific to the PNR-fail context or reflects general PULL_UP efficiency or shot-quality differences.
own_inferences: The question is testable at the defensive-team-season level (about 30 teams x 4 seasons, or fewer if the 2025-26 partial data is excluded), but per-unit PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP cell counts may be small, so many units may fail a minimum-count gate.

Median lift over more than 2pp plus a 70% positive rate is a high bar that could be met by a shot-quality artifact (PULL_UP is a long-two or three-point shot with a mechanical PPP floor). The baseline must control for shot value and distance.
Using a 2pp threshold on raw PPP without a matched baseline is likely to fail or to produce an artifact, given the shrinkage in SF-APPA-067.
uncertainties: The operational definition of 'PNR fail' is not in the task or the records (for example a turnover, a missed shot, or a defined possession outcome).
How 'lift' is defined (PPP difference, versus a baseline PPP, versus a matched expectation) and what the baseline is.
Cell counts per unit, and whether units are defensive teams, defender-lineups, or team x PT.
Whether 2025-26 regular season data (complete from 2026-04-13) and playoff data (partial until 2026-06-21) are used. Only complete data should be used for the primary test.
The retrieved records do not state their n for PNR-fail-PULL_UP cells, and the status values carry no pass/fail result.
Whether the 70% and 2pp thresholds were set before any data was seen (no pre-registration record was retrieved).

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval showed that earlier counter and suppression claims in this project were descriptive, or shrank under controls or were flagged for placebo dependence and label error. Those findings lower the chance that an unadjusted lift rule would hold, so the question should not proceed as a raw threshold test. Instead it should proceed only with a pre-specified PNR-fail definition, a matched baseline and placebo/falsification checks, with the 70%/2pp rule applied to adjusted lift.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR-fail and PULL_UP tagging from play-by-play may be inconsistent with the PNR proxy used elsewhere; the earlier PNR share jump was flagged as possibly a tagging difference.
Per-unit PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP possession counts may be too small for stable unit-level lift, especially at team x PT or lineup granularity.
Shot quality, opponent quality, and game context can produce PULL_UP lift after PNR fail without any counter effect.
PULL_UP PPP is bounded by shot value and make rates, so positive lift over baseline may reflect shot-type mix rather than a counter.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests whether PULL_UP lift after PNR fail is positive in at least 70% of units with median lift above 2pp. Related descriptive PNR and PULL_UP PPP and share summaries exist (SF-APPS-012, SF-APPM-058). Related counter and suppression claims (SF-CHT-009, SF-APPA-067) shrank under robustness checks or were flagged as placebo-dependent. The question is therefore partly addressed in descriptive form and not in the conditional inferential form posed.

risks.text: PNR-fail and PULL_UP labels derive from play-by-play tagging. The retrieved records flag tagging differences as a possible explanation for PNR share shifts (SF-APPS-012).
If PNR fail is defined from the possession's outcome (for example a turnover or a missed shot), the trigger and the outcome are not independent, so lift will be inflated.
PULL_UP efficiency is bounded by shot value and make rate, so a lift above baseline may reflect shot-type mix (SF-APPS-012 also flagged this).
Opponent quality, lineup, and game state can drive both PNR fail and PULL_UP efficiency.
Unit-level cell counts for PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP may be small, making the 70% and median rules unstable.
Many defensive units may have few PNR-fail possessions followed by PULL_UP, so units may fail a minimum-count gate.
Similar star or forced-play-type gaps in SF-CHT-009 were treated as artifacts once sequence work was added, so a single contrast is unreliable without placebo play types.
Scanning multiple play-type pairs and unit definitions for a lift rule raises the false-positive rate.
Units selected for extreme PNR-fail rates or extreme PULL_UP lift may regress toward the mean in subsequent seasons.
Play-type frequencies and shot-quality profiles changed across 2022-23 to 2025-26, and the playoff sample is partial at the time of the question.

design.estimand: Within defensive units, the mean difference in PPP between PULL_UP possessions that follow a PNR-fail trigger and matched baseline PULL_UP possessions not preceded by PNR fail, adjusted for shot distance/type, opponent quality, and game state. The rule is evaluated on the share of units with adjusted lift>0 and the median adjusted lift.
design.unit: Defensive team x season (primary), with team x season x playoff/regular-season as a secondary stratum. Units with fewer than a pre-specified minimum of PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP possessions are excluded and reported.
design.sample: Regular season 2022-23 to 2024-25 and 2025-26 regular season only after completion (from 2026-04-13). Playoffs are excluded from the primary test (the 2025-26 playoffs are partial and not final). Playoffs are a secondary sensitivity check with 2023-24 and 2024-25 complete data.
design.power: To be computed before analysis from the observed per-unit PNR-fail-PULL_UP counts in the 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons. If fewer than about 20 units meet the minimum-count gate, the test is reported as underpowered, not as a result.
design.controls: Adjust for shot distance and type, expected PPP from league-wide shot-quality tables, opponent offensive strength, lineup or rotation context, and game state (score, period, clock). Compare PNR-fail-PULL_UP to a matched baseline of PULL_UP possessions from the same defensive unit and shot-quality bin, not to all possessions. Use shrinkage (e.g., empirical Bayes) on unit-level lift to address noisy small cells.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo trigger: the same PULL_UP comparison after non-PNR actions (e.g., ISO fail or spot-up fail); lift should be near zero. (2) Placebo outcome: the PNR-fail effect on non-PULL_UP shot types should not show the same pattern. (3) Split-half stability: lift sign and median should agree across seasons. (4) Tagging check: PNR-fail labels validated against a hand-coded sample.
design.multiplicity: One pre-specified primary rule (share of units with adjusted lift>0 and median adjusted lift >2pp). Other play types and definitions are secondary, with Holm adjustment across them. Thresholds are fixed before analysis.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if (a) at least 70% of eligible units have adjusted lift>0, (b) the median adjusted lift exceeds 2pp, (c) the placebo trigger shows no comparable lift, and (d) the result holds in both regular-season halves. Rejected if (a) or (b) fails with adequate power. Artifact if the lift disappears after shot-quality adjustment or appears in placebo triggers. Otherwise uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA stats API play-by-play, substitution intervals and matchup files for 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13. Playoffs excluded from primary test. Derived Neo4j play-type possession records version to be frozen and logged before analysis.

methodological_questions: Does PULL_UP lift exceed 0 in at least 70% of units with median lift above 2pp, conditional on PNR fail?
How should units, lift, and PNR-fail conditioning be defined and tested with play-by-play derived possession records?
args.query: PNR fail then PULL_UP counter league-wide lift by unit, defensive suppression counter strategy, play-type possession records, lift threshold 2pp and 70% of units

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
